title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** 

Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: extrajudicial kidnappings have no place in our country. The USA is a nation founded on free speech, due process, and liberty. We will gather to demand the end of extrajudicial kidnappings by ICE and the Trump administration.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

_A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values._
accessibility_notes: Primary location is the sidewalk in front of the large federal courthouse building. No onsite parking is available; no public restrooms are available.

title: Solidarity Breakfast and Shopping in the Sunnyside neighborhood, Canton
description:
Saturday afternoon (6/7) ICE raided Canton’s Sunnyside neighborhood -- OUR community--with a fleet of dark unmarked cars and fully-masked federal agents. The images and videos are chilling. No warrants. No due process. Just shadowy para-military figures “disappearing” people.

Multiple businesses closed for the weekend out of fear for themselves, employees, and patrons.

We can Do Something to support our neighbors in Sunnyside! Join Latino Outreach of Cherokee County for a tasty bite to eat at La Luna Bakery and Deli, followed by shopping at local stores in the area for groceries, clothing, DVDs, snacks and meals.

Save your grocery shopping for this event and join us to show solidarity with this important community!

title: Town of Gorham Democratic Caucus
description:
# Caucus Meeting

## Meeting begins at 7:00
### Arrive early to check in 

### What is a caucus meeting? 
It is the opportunity for Democrats living in the Town of Gorham to select their candidates for this November's general election.

### What offices need candidates?
1. Supervisor (term 3 yr)
2. Council Member (2 offices, term 3 yrs)
3. Clerk (term 3 yrs)
4. Highway Superintendent (term 3 yrs)
5. Town Tax Collector (term 3 yrs)

### Who can participate?
Only registered voters enrolled in the Democratic Party and living in the Town of Gorham can participate in the meeting. 
Participation means: making motions, nominations and seconds, speaking in discussions and voting on potential candidates.

### Who can attend?
Any member of the public can attend this meeting.

title: Franklin Township, NJ: Rally to Stop The NESE Pipeline
description:
The NESE pipeline is BACK. **Trump wants to fast-track this dangerous polluting project here in Central Jersey — and we need your help to stop it again!**

On Thursday evening, the Franklin Township Council will consider a resolution opposing NESE once again. Join us to rally at 6 p.m. in front of the Franklin Municipal Complex (at the gazebo) ahead of the meeting to show strong opposition to this zombie project.

Municipal resolutions send a powerful message to the Governor and other decision-makers and are an effective way to push for change at the local level. **Join us to speak out against this un-NESE-sary pipeline!**


### About NESE:

The Northeast Supply Enhancement (NESE) proposal calls for construction of a gas-powered gas compressor station in Franklin Township, as well as 3.5 miles of connecting pipeline through Old Bridge and 23 miles of new pipeline under the Raritan Bay / New York Harbor.

NESE would pollute our water, increase flooding, destroy critical wetlands and habitats, and would cut through the already-polluted and sensitive Raritan Bay and New York Bay. Pipelines leak enormous amounts of methane, a stronger greenhouse gas than CO2, which directly contributes to climate change.

The proposed compressor station in Franklin would release air- and water-polluting toxins. The gases emitted by a compressor station can increase the risk of asthma as well as cardiovascular, neurological, developmental, and respiratory diseases.

This project is not in the public interest for New Jersey residents. Our communities in New Jersey will receive the direct impacts of pipeline leakage and compressor station pollution, while none of the gas is even for New Jersey.

**We defeated NESE last year, and we can do it again. Join us as we get organized and rally against zombie NESE!**

title: Solidarity Restaurants Launch
description:
Restaurant workers are under attack from multiple directions. Restaurants are the largest employers of immigrants and one of the first locations for ICE raids, but restaurant workers also use Medicaid and food stamps at double the rate of other workers because of their inhumanly low wages. That means millions who serve us food are about to lose these health care benefits, creating a public health disaster. 

Over 100 restaurant owners from across the country have come together to launch Solidarity Restaurants - pledging to stand by their employees and calling on elected officials to respect their dignity, human rights, and contributions to our industry and our nation. These employers are committed to providing safe, sustainable, livable wages and working conditions to all of our employees.

Join us for a delicious brunch and come see Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Maria Hinojosa as she interviews these amazing restaurant owners - stand with them and their employer at the launch of Solidarity Restaurants !

title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

description: The Santa Fe chapter of Veterans For Peace started this vigil in 2002 and have continued it every Friday at noon for 23 years. Its purpose is to bring awareness to the hundreds of billions of our tax dollars going to the production of new nuclear weapons here in our state. Many people, even many New Mexicans, are unaware that Los Alamos National Lab is currently building several new bomb factories to increase production of nuclear bomb cores (known as plutonium "pits") to reach a goal of 30 to 120 new pits per year. Loud public outcry may be able to halt this waste of federal money, or at least slow it down until we elect a saner administration. Life on Earth is at stake.

title: Working Class Workshops
description:
Hello future candidates! Ready to take the next step to get ready for your campaign? Welcome to Working Class Workshops, your week-long training and workshop sessions that will keep your momentum moving toward victory. These sessions are built to be equal parts learning and application, as we discuss campaign fundamentals such as fundraising, narrative, social media, and the kinds of campaigns needed to win governing power for the working class of all races. Excited to keep learning? Sign up for our virtual sessions and let’s get to work!  

The schedule of trainings are as follows [each session will be held virtually at 6:30PM - 8:30PM CDT]: 

Monday, June 23rd: Building Independent Political Power
This session will be exploring WFP’s theory regarding how to build governing power for the working class of all races and what we believe about elections, candidates and the role of a political party. 

Tuesday, June 24th: Communications: Message and Narrative
This session will be teaching and workshopping with participants the best skills and practices for authentically connecting our individual stories to a larger narrative that fuels the messages that a campaign will be communicating to their voters.  

Wednesday, June 25th: Past Candidates and Current Electeds Panel
This session will be centered around the experiences, guidance and wisdom that our panel of former candidates and current elected leaders will share with participants. 

Thursday, June 26th: Finding and Funding Our Why
This session will be grounded in fundraising principles and tactics - while using concepts learned in Communications: Message and Narrative to construct commonly used tools such as elevator pitches, life lists, and making a strong fundraising ask.

Friday, June 27th: Social Media Workshop
This session will be teaching participants how to strategically use social media as an effective campaign and messaging tool, including mythbreaking common misconceptions about social media platforms, tips for candidates and campaign staff, and relatable examples of campaigns using social media to their highest potential.
